clues: This town sits in the north west of a long land in South America. It stands by a river, close to where the river meets the vast sea.
This town stands in a dry desert, yet its air feels like spring all year long. A great sea stream off the coast helps keep the days mild and the rain light.
In 1824, a great war chief made this town the chief town of its land for a time. He did this to help the land win free of Spain.
Just by this town stands the largest old city built of sun dried mud in the world. Its walls rose long ago, well before the Inca ruled here.
This town is famed as the home of a proud folk dance of its land. Each year, a big fest for that dance draws folk from far and wide.
